cnn.title: Nvidia rules out return for disgraced boss
cnn.desc:
Jensen Huang fails in his bid to be re-hired as CEO of Nvidia after a scandal over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating whether the company misled investors. Nvidia has meanwhile reported a doubling of revenues during his last quarter in charge.Also: President Donald Trump is attending a regional economic summit in China, a day ahead of a historic meeting with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, and the Russian leader, Vladimir Putin, in the city of Shenzhen. The US has lost its measles-free status and infections are continuing to spread. Researchers have been learning more about humpback whales by using drones to collect their snot. We have a report from the West Bank after a 72-year-old Palestinian woman was shot dead by armed settlers in Jericho. New research has found that genes inherited from Neanderthals can reduce the risk of schizophrenia. A Georgia O'Keefe painting that was hidden in a cupboard for years has sold at auction for 4.8 million dollars. And the spacecraft Voyager 1 will clock up a milestone - reaching a distance of one light day from earth.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Special episode: Trump, Putin and Xi meeting
cnn.desc:
This special episode of the Global News Podcast brings together our China specialist, our North America correspondent, and our Russia and Ukraine analyst, to discuss an unprecedented summit taking place this week.
The US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, China, for their first-ever trilateral talks. President Trump has said the agenda will include denuclearisation, the war with Iran, and the war in Ukraine. So what could emerge from this meeting? Some analysts are hopeful that China could exert some influence on Tehran, and act as a mediator between Moscow and Kyiv. But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he's worried that the three leaders could try to reshape the international order as they see fit, without consulting smaller countries. Trump, Putin and Xi are also expected to talk about the economy and AI, particularly after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of Nvidia, following allegations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But will any big decisions come out of the talks in Shenzhen? Or is this about symbolism: a way for the leaders of China, the US and Russia to give themselves a boost and a distraction from their problems at home? cnn.title: OpenAI sued by California over rogue cyber attacks
cnn.desc:
The California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI, alleging the ChatGPT maker misled the public and put people at risk by developing AI models without adequate safeguards. The lawsuit cites the July 2026 attack on the AI platform Hugging Face, in which experimental OpenAI agents accessed the internet and breached the company's internal systems. An OpenAI spokesperson told the BBC that the lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab".Also: Five European countries have announced plans to set up immigration "return hubs" in Rwanda. Robert Pattinson has been named as the new James Bond.  Russia and Ukraine have launched major attacks on each other, destroying three key bridges. A forensic expert has told the BBC he believes Jeffrey Epstein's death was the result of a homicide, not suicide. And controversy in South Africa over the removal of wild baboons from Cape Town.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Crimea Kerch Bridge hit in a huge Ukrainian drone attack
cnn.desc:
The Russian defence ministry says a record number of drones were fired from Ukraine overnight and more than 1300 were brought down by its air defences. An oil refinery in the Krasnodar region was targeted and there was damage to the Kerch Bridge which links Russia to occupied Crimea. Western countries call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza. The Indonesian president apologises to neighbouring countries for the thick haze caused by massive forest fires in his country. The director of the Shakespeare Institute threatens to resign if plans to move the centre from Stratford-upon-Avon to Birmingham go ahead. And could co-founder Jensen Huang make a swift return to the US technology giant, Nvidia?

cnn.title: Government forces retreat in Yemen
cnn.desc:
Yemen's Saudi-backed government has been redeploying its forces to protect its temporary capital, Aden, after advances by the Houthi movement which is backed by Iran. They've withdrawn from an area overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait at the entrance to the Red Sea. It signalled the end of a six-week counter offensive to retake coastal territory from the Houthis, whose control over the Yemeni side of the Strait has further constrained Middle East oil exports. Also: the architect of Mexico's cocaine trade Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies at the age of 80. Guatemala declares 30-day state of emergency amid drug trafficking violence in the eastern districts of Zacapa and Izabal. WHO research published in Lancet Global Health finds one in four teenagers worldwide has not been physically active for at least 60 minutes on any day in the previous week. Taliban authorities ban cricket on Kandahar radio. Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine. Canadian Stephanie Case becomes the first woman to complete the Antarctic Ice Ultra Marathon. And how London-based typewriter poet Olivia Dodd connects with strangers.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: The Global Story: How North Korea pulled off a $6bn heist
cnn.desc: Last week saw what could be the biggest heist in history: $6.3bn was stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. North Korean hackers are suspected of being behind the attack, which saw billions of dollars disappear in just 20 minutes. It’s far from the first time North Korea has been accused of a major cyber-attack. Over the past decade, hackers linked to the country have targeted banks, public institutions and even Sony Pictures. On The Global Story, Asma Khalid speaks with journalist Geoff White, host of the BBC investigative podcast The Lazarus Heist. He explains how this isolated country become a major player in the world of cyber-crime – and where all that money goes. The Global Story brings clarity to politics, business and foreign policy in a time of connection and disruption. For more episodes, just search 'The Global Story' wherever you get your BBC Podcasts.

cnn.title: SpaceX makes history catching part of returning spacecraft
cnn.desc:
Part of SpaceX's Starship rocket was caught as it descended back to Earth in Texas. It's the first time the upper section of a reusable rocket has ever been captured. Mechanical arms carried out a "chopstick" manoeuvre to catch the spacecraft. The breakthrough could dramatically cut the cost of space travel and marks a major step towards making Starship suitable for human spaceflight.Also: Ukraine's president says the US has, for the first time, floated the idea of Ukraine joining NATO in exchange for ceding control of the Donbas region to Russia. We hear from the first black senator of the US state of Mississippi in 145 years. A fierce debate is brewing in Germany over the future of Hitler's Eagle's Nest after the building was destroyed by fire. A leading specialist in detecting digitally manipulated images warns that deepfakes are becoming almost impossible to spot. And a Philippine teenager has won the first-ever Eurovision Asia competition.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: The Happy Pod: I've put women on the map with Antarctic record
cnn.desc:
Before taking on Antarctica's 160 kilometre ultramarathon, Stephanie Case said she wanted to show her daughter what mothers can achieve even in the toughest places on Earth. The Canadian ultra-runner has now made history, becoming the first woman to complete the race. Case says she wanted to prove that ''motherhood isn't the finish line''.Also: we catch up with a young Sudanese boy who received a surprise message from his favourite footballer, the Real Madrid player Vinícius Júnior. We visit a drama workshop where actors use sound to create theatre for blind and visually impaired people. How robotic kits with chopsticks are inspiring children around the world. The African athletes who have made history at the Youth Olympic Games in Senegal. Plus the chimpanzee in Florida that had his own drone delivery service of bananas.(Photo: Stephanie Case pictured after completing the Antarctic Ice Ultra 2026. Credit: Reuters)Presenter: Chantal Hartle. 
Music composed by Iona Hampson

cnn.title: US airspace reopens after flights grounded for several hours
cnn.desc:
On Friday, the US made the rare decision to ground flights nationwide, leaving tens of thousands of people stranded. An overloaded air traffic control system triggered communications failures across the country. The White House says there's no evidence of a cyberattack. Flights resumed after four hours, but Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has warned that getting the aviation network back to normal will take time.Also: Divisions deepen inside the Trump administration as the US Commerce Secretary comes under criticism for his failure to ban exports of advanced Nvidia chips to a company linked to a suspected Chinese spy. Microsoft says its services are gradually returning to normal after a global outage that affected hundreds of millions of people. Pope Leo says he's overcoming cancer as huge crowds turn out to welcome him in Peru. We report from India, where members of the Gen-Z "Cockroach" protest movement face growing legal pressure and detentions. And the grand final of the first-ever Asian Eurovision Song Contest is about to get underway.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Microsoft outage: Millions affected in over 70 countries
cnn.desc:
A global Microsoft outage hits schools, doctors and businesses. The tech giant is scrambling to fix the issue - but with so many of us relying on its products such as Outlook and Teams, it has prompted a conversation about how reliant we are on its services. Microsoft says it's not found any evidence that malicious activity caused the problems, and in its latest update it reported that "broader improvements" were being observed in North America and Europe. Also: El Salvador soldiers use combat robot dogs equipped with assault rifles to re-take the national football stadium from gangs in Haiti. The FBI says North Korean hackers used fake video calls in a 400-million dollar crypto hack. Mauricio Pochettino is finally confirmed as Manchester United's new manager. cnn.title: Putin lets Europe join Ukraine peace talks
cnn.desc:
Ukraine's President Zelensky has welcomed efforts by Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to secure European involvement at the next round of peace talks with Russia. He was speaking alongside the US envoys in Dublin, where they'd flown to brief Mr Zelensky on their earlier discussions with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Mr Zelensky said it made sense for Europeans to be involved as Ukraine would eventually be an EU member.Also: One of the most powerful men in the AI industry -Jensen Huang- will appear before Congress in the US after being forced to resign over a sex and spying scandal. Schools in Italy have been evacuated for a second day in a row after receiving hoax bomb threats. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group for laughing at Arlington National Cemetery. Haiti's security forces say they've regained control of the country’s main stadium in the capital Port au Prince, which has held by gangs for two years. How Pakistan is leading the way in solar energy... and, as matcha continues to boom, a new Japanese matcha congress meets to try and stop it being a victim of its own success.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens.
